newsitem.title: USA: Coastal moves ahead on products pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Coastal moves ahead on products pipeline.

text.p: Coastal Corp said Thursday its subsidiaries have completed acquisition of right-of-way for a 134-mile petroleum products pipeline from Corpus Christi, Texas, to the site of a proposed products terminal at Edinburg in the Lower Rio Grande Valley of Texas.

Coastal also said that its subsidiaries have acquired a 17-acre site just north of Edinburg for construction of the terminal. Regulatory applications for the terminal construction have been filed, and engineering work is under way for both the pipeline and terminal construction.

"When this project is fully developed, it will provide a reliable, economic and environmentally sound outlet of refined petroleum products from refineries in Corpus Christi to the growing Texas Rio Grande Valley," said chief executive David A. Arledge.
Currently more than 80 percent of petroleum products delivered to the Rio Grande Valley must be barged through the Intracoastal Waterway and then trucked to inland markets, Coastal pointed out.
For many years, Coastal has operated a smaller products pipeline from Corpus Christi to Hidalgo, Texas, near the Mexican border.

Once the new pipeline to Edinburg is in operation, the company said, it plans to refurbish and convert the smaller, existing pipeline to propane service and extend the pipeline to the border to a new propane terminal serving the expanding local markets.

Coastal also said it plans to convert part of its existing pipeline network to gather and transport increasing production of crude oil from its share of the Jeffress Field in South Texas to refineries in Corpus Christi.
